newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: WMC could raise copper output - report.
newsitem.headline: WMC could raise copper output - report.

text.p: WMC Ltd could invest a further A$900 million to raise annual production at its Olympic Dam mine in South Australia to 350,000 tonnes of copper and 7,900 tonnes of uranium, the Adelaide Advertiser reported on Friday.
The newspaper quoted WMC managing director Hugh Morgan as saying WMC had no present commitment to increase output beyond the already planned A$1.48 billion expansion at Olympic Dam.
However, he said the company had prepared an environmental impact statement seeking approval to quadruple current production, the report said.

Morgan was quoted as saying the expansion plan described in the environmental statement would require an investment of A$900 million beginning in 2008 and would bring the total investment at Olympic Dam to about A$3.5 billion.

"If Olympic Dam is to maintain its international competitiveness in the years ahead it must become a large volume producer," Morgan was quoted as telling a luncheon sponsored by the South Australian Chamber of Mines and Energy.
The state government of South Australia announced in October legislative changes to allow expansion of copper production at Olympic Dam to up to 350,000 tonnes.
